words: Some people say the text is pushed to the left in a strange way that makes no sense.

diagnosis.summary: There is no single switch behind this complaint. The forced direction itself is sound: after I18nManager.forceRTL a JavaScript reload is enough on both platforms (Android re-reads the flag at every root measure, iOS when the reloaded surface builds its view), with one real hole: English chosen on an Arabic-language iPhone stays right-to-left for ever. What members see as "text thrown to the left" comes from text rules: both platforms take a paragraph's direction from its first strong letter (Arabic that opens with a Latin word reads backwards; on Android every Arabic paragraph of a multi-line message whose first line opens Latin is drawn on the left; on iPhone any unaligned Text that opens Latin is drawn from the left), three text boxes carry the Text helper textStart (physical left for a TextInput), and the "own letters" rule sends Latin-only strings to the left edge. Today's pass cured part of it (contact box, projects search, project cards on iPhone) but spread that last rule to projects, videos and advisor replies, where it now also pushes Latin names left on Android.

causes.cause: Text boxes styled with the Text helper `textStart` ('left'). A Text reads 'left' as the start edge (right in Arabic); a TextInput reads it as the physical left. So the placeholder and the typed Arabic sit on the left while everything around them is on the right.
causes.evidence: Helper: C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\i18n\direction.ts:29 (`textStart = 'left'`), :47-49 (`inputStart()` is the physical one). Native: Android C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\node_modules\react-native\ReactAndroid\src\main\java\com\facebook\react\views\textinput\ReactTextInputManager.kt:545-568 (`"left" -> Gravity.LEFT`, no RTL swap). iOS: an input's attributes carry no layoutDirection (C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\node_modules\react-native\ReactCommon\react\renderer\components\textinput\BaseTextInputProps.cpp:230-244), so the left/right swap in ...\textlayoutmanager\platform\ios\react\renderer\textlayoutmanager\RCTAttributedTextUtils.mm:198-207 never runs for it. Members' bundle (git show 97705af): app/src/components/CountryPicker.tsx:157-165 (search, `textAlign: textStart`), app/src/components/OptionPicker.tsx:126, app/src/app/contact.tsx:220; app/src/app/(tabs)/projects.tsx:91-101 with style :265 had no alignment at all. Sequence: Arabic app -> sign-in or sign-up -> tap the country -> the sheet opens with autoFocus -> «ابحث بالاسم أو رمز الاتصال…» and the typed letters are at the left edge; same in the «راسل الإدارة» composer and the city picker of the affiliate form. Working tree: C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\contact.tsx:234 and C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\(tabs)\projects.tsx:102 are fixed; C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\components\CountryPicker.tsx:165-173 and C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\components\OptionPicker.tsx:130 are unchanged. The reviewers saw the same thing on the emulator for contact.tsx (C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\docs\reviews\2026-11-15\rev-home.md:51).
causes.platforms: iOS and Android, Arabic mode, every version (1.2.0 to 1.3.3)
causes.fixedToday: partly: contact composer and projects search fixed; the country search (sign-in, sign-up, profile, WhatsApp check) and the option search are not

causes.cause: Android: a Text holding several lines gets ONE alignment, computed from the first strong letter of the whole string, but applied to each paragraph relative to that paragraph's own direction. If the first line opens with a Latin word, every Arabic paragraph under it is drawn on the LEFT; inside an Arabic message, any line that opens Latin or holds only digits or a link is drawn on the left.
causes.evidence: C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\node_modules\react-native\ReactAndroid\src\main\java\com\facebook\react\views\text\TextLayoutManager.kt:184-214 (`isScriptRTL` = first strong letter of the whole spanned; one Layout.Alignment; NORMAL and OPPOSITE swapped when it differs from the layout direction) and :661-694 (StaticLayout built with setAlignment only, no setTextDirection, so each paragraph resolves its own direction by first strong letter). An explicit `textAlign: textStart` does not change this (it is the same branch as no alignment). Sites that print server or member text with line breaks in one Text: C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\contact.tsx:176 (the management thread, including the message opened to every account in M241), C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\components\AdminPopup.tsx:85, C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\components\WorkshopAd.tsx:108, C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\(tabs)\news.tsx:157, C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\meetup\[key].tsx:49, C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\people\[id].tsx:68 (bio). Sequence: the management writes «Investors Club» on the first line (the brand rule keeps the name Latin) and Arabic lines below -> on Android the Arabic lines hug the left edge; on iPhone they stay right because the explicit alignment is applied to the whole string (RCTAttributedTextUtils.mm:198-207). Same files and lines in 97705af.
causes.platforms: Android only, both languages (mirror image in English), every version

causes.cause: iPhone: a Text with no textAlign is aligned by iOS from its first strong letter. Content that opens with a Latin word (a brand, an English name) or holds only digits, and fills the row width, is drawn from the left edge in left-to-right order, between right-aligned Arabic neighbours.
causes.evidence: React Native sets no paragraph alignment when the style has none (C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\node_modules\react-native\ReactCommon\react\renderer\textlayoutmanager\platform\ios\react\renderer\textlayoutmanager\RCTAttributedTextUtils.mm:198-216), which leaves it to TextKit's natural alignment; Android instead aligns such text to the layout start (TextLayoutManager.kt:197-203), so Android members do not see this one. The project's own notes describe it: C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\i18n\direction.ts:36-38 (M177) and C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\docs\reviews\2026-11-15\rev-projects.md:42. Members' bundle (97705af), full-width text with no alignment and live content: app/src/components/ProjectCard.tsx:84, :90, :95 (title, company, excerpt), app/src/app/project/[id].tsx:116 (title), :126 (English title), :350 (description paragraphs, style `body` :429), app/src/components/PostsBlock.tsx:77 and :112 (styles :163-164), app/src/components/GoldenCompanyCard.tsx:34-36. Working tree: ProjectCard.tsx:87-98 and project/[id].tsx:120, :130 now take `textDir`; still unaligned: C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\project\[id].tsx:367 (style `body` :446), C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\components\PostsBlock.tsx:77, :112, C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\components\GoldenCompanyCard.tsx:35-37. Scan: 249 of 730 text styles carry no textAlign; most sit in rows or pills where it cannot show, 59 usages are stretched (62 in the members' tree).
causes.fixedToday: partly: Projects Bank cards and the project title; not the project description, the posts block, the golden company cards

causes.cause: Both platforms: an Arabic sentence that opens with a Latin word gets a left-to-right base direction, so the Latin word is drawn at the left end and the full stop at the right end even when the block is right-aligned. The app's cure (`writingDirection` from `textDir`) works on iOS only.
causes.evidence: Android ignores the style: C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\node_modules\react-native\ReactAndroid\src\main\java\com\facebook\react\views\text\TextAttributeProps.kt:417 (`TA_KEY_BEST_WRITING_DIRECTION -> {}`), and the layout uses the default first-strong rule (TextLayoutManager.kt:661-694). iOS applies it only where it is passed (RCTAttributedTextUtils.mm:212-216); `textDir` is C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\i18n\direction.ts:40-44. The bundled Arabic copy is clean (2 of 1,614 strings open with a Latin letter: auth.login.placeholder, form.file.hint; the brand sits mid-sentence everywhere), so this is live content: project excerpts and descriptions, posts, advisor replies, dashboard texts, hub sentences, member bios.

Members have it in the news only; today's pass spread it to projects, videos, the player, advisor replies and file names, where Latin names used to sit on the right.

In 97705af only: app/src/app/news/[id].tsx:64, :71, app/src/components/NewsCarousel.tsx:208, :234, :235, app/src/components/news/NewsCard.tsx:60, :64. Added in 0fcf3e5: C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\components\ProjectCard.tsx:87, :93, :98; ProjectsBankCarousel.tsx:86; GoldenOpportunity.tsx:91; C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\project\[id].tsx:120, :130; VideoCard.tsx:61, :65; C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\watch.tsx:93; C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\components\advisor\RichText.tsx:18-21, Composer.tsx:54, MessageBubble.tsx:146. causes.cause: iPhone only: English chosen on an iPhone whose language is Arabic stays right-to-left at every launch. The member sees English text hugging the right, mirrored rows, while chevrons and inputs follow the left-to-right helpers.
causes.evidence:
iOS direction = forceRTL OR (allowRTL AND the app's language is right-to-left): C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app
ode_moduleseact-native\React\Modules\RCTI18nUtil.m:32-41, :99-103. The binary ships ar.lproj (C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\app.config.ts:117), so the last term is true on an Arabic iPhone. The patched expo-localization still calls `allowRTL(true)` in OnCreate (C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app
ode_modules\expo-localization\ios\LocalizationModule.swift:23-31, :72), and every Expo module is created at every start and every reload (C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app
ode_modules\expo-modules-core\ios\Core\ModuleHolder.swift:56). Sequence: «حسابي» -> English -> C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\i18n\direction.ts:97-104 writes allowRTL(false), forceRTL(false) and reloads -> the reload re-allows RTL -> the layout is RTL again -> syncDirection (:82-94) restarts once, the same happens, the guard at :91 returns -> English in a right-to-left layout, and the same at every later launch (the guard key is never cleared). Android is not affected: its direction needs the force flag (I18nUtil.kt:22-24; the device-language term at :63-69 reads Locale.getAvailableLocales()[0], not the phone's language). The patch dates from 2026-10-23, so every binary from 1.2.0 behaves this way.
causes.platforms: iOS, English mode on an Arabic-language iPhone, 1.2.0 to 1.3.3

causes.cause: Android: the direction flag is live, the language is not. The flag is flipped before the reload is requested; if the reload waits, the old-language screen can be re-laid out in the new direction (Arabic to English: Arabic text in a left-to-right layout). Related edge: the 12-second launch watchdog opens the app in the default Arabic before the saved language is read.
causes.evidence: The root re-reads the flag at every measure: C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\node_modules\react-native\ReactAndroid\src\main\java\com\facebook\react\runtime\ReactSurfaceView.kt:83-117 -> ReactSurfaceImpl.kt:178-194, :217. direction.ts:97-104 flips the flag, then asks for the reload; expo-updates runs its procedures one at a time (C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\node_modules\expo-updates\android\src\main\java\expo\modules\updates\statemachine\UpdatesStateMachine.kt:46-48), and C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\app\_layout.tsx:137-155 downloads an update in the first 30 seconds of a launch (always the case on a fresh install), so a language change from the welcome screen in that window waits for the download. A root re-measure in between (keyboard) flips the layout. Watchdog: _layout.tsx:57, :176-182 with the default `lang = 'ar'` at C:\Projects\vibes-club-app\app\src\i18n\index.ts:40. Both windows are narrow.
causes.platforms: Android (the watchdog edge on both), every version

fixPlan.change: Text boxes: in the `search` style of both pickers replace `textAlign: textStart` with `textAlign: inputStart(), writingDirection: isRTL() ? 'rtl' : 'ltr'` (the same lines as contact.tsx:234; both sheets use the lazy `themedStyles`, so the call is made at render time). Add one line to the lint script: `textStart` / `textEnd` never in a style passed to a TextInput.
fixPlan.risk: Low. Two style lines; check the sheet in Arabic and in English on the emulator.

fixPlan.change: One primitive for every server- or member-written string. In direction.ts add `dirMark(paragraph)`: U+200F in front of a paragraph that holds an Arabic letter, U+200E otherwise (the mark is what Android obeys; `writingDirection` stays for iOS). Add a `ContentText` component that splits the string on line breaks, renders one Text per paragraph (with `numberOfLines` it joins the lines with a space instead), and applies the mark, the writing direction and the alignment. Use it at: contact.tsx:176, AdminPopup.tsx:85, WorkshopAd.tsx:108, (tabs)/news.tsx:157, meetup/[key].tsx:49, people/[id].tsx:68, hq/index.tsx:194, requests/index.tsx:154, PostsBlock.tsx:77 and :112, GoldenCompanyCard.tsx:35-37, project/[id].tsx:345-367 (through Highlight), golden/[code].tsx:99-111, StructuredText and advisor RichText paragraphs, and the 20 current `textDir` sites. This cures the Android paragraph rule, the reversed word order on Android and the unaligned text on iPhone in one place.

The invisible mark must stay at index 0 when Highlight and SarText split the string, must not reach anything sent to the server or compared as text, and travels with copied text. ClampText measuring and `numberOfLines` previews need a look. Needs one emulator pass in both languages and one look on an iPhone.

fixPlan.change: Decide the alignment rule for Latin-only content in Arabic mode. Recommended: every string stays on the start edge (right in Arabic, left in English) and only the reading order follows its letters, i.e. `textDir()` returns `textAlign: textStart` with the content's writing direction; own-side alignment only for full English paragraphs if the owner wants it (news body, a long advisor reply). This undoes the left jump of Latin titles at the 13 sites added today (project cards, project page, videos, player, golden opportunity, carousel, advisor, file names) and still cures the M177 case, because an Arabic headline that opens with a Latin word becomes right-to-left and right-aligned. Decide before today's bundle is published.

fixPlan.change: Default alignment for the remaining unaligned text: add `textAlign: textStart` to the six typography tokens (tokens.ts:250-255) so every style that spreads a token starts from the start edge unless it sets its own, and give the styles that do not use a token an explicit one (PostsBlock.tsx:163-164, GoldenCompanyCard code/name/tagline, project/[id].tsx:446). Keep the scan used in this step as a lint check (text style with a font and no textAlign, used in a column container).

fixPlan.change: Make the layout follow the loaded language even when the native flag disagrees: give the root container at _layout.tsx:204 `direction: isRTL() ? 'rtl' : 'ltr'`. Text alignment follows the Yoga direction of its own node on both platforms (ParagraphShadowNode.cpp:78-84), so this covers English on an Arabic iPhone, the Android window between the flag and the reload, and the watchdog launch, on every runtime already installed.

Either drop `supportsRTL` from the plugin options and from `extra` (app.config.ts:134 and :177), which makes the module's OnCreate a no-op on both platforms, or extend the existing patch to remove LocalizationModule.swift:72. The app's own allowRTL / forceRTL then persist. Android keeps `android:supportsRtl="true"` from the Expo template (checked in expo/template.tgz and in the local prebuild manifest).

notVerified: Nothing was run on an iPhone. That iOS draws an unaligned Text from its first strong letter is TextKit behaviour: React Native's source only shows that no alignment is set; the project's own M177 note and rev-projects.md:42 describe the same symptom.

The iPhone reload path (RCTHost.mm:621-644 -> RCTFabricSurface.mm:80-85, :142-156, :177-190) and the English-on-Arabic-iPhone lock were read from source only. One device check settles it: Arabic-language iPhone, choose English, close and reopen twice.

Which of these the complaining members actually saw: there are no member screenshots, and how many live projects, posts and messages open with a Latin word was not measured (no network calls in this step).

diagnosis.data:
WHEN THE NATIVE DIRECTION CHANGES
iOS: isRTL = forceRTL OR (allowRTL AND the app's language is right-to-left) - RCTI18nUtil.m:32-41. Read from NSUserDefaults when the surface builds its view (RCTFabricSurface.mm:142-156, :177-190). expo-updates reloadAsync -> RCTTriggerReloadCommandListeners (RelaunchProcedure.swift:76) -> RCTHost resets and restarts every surface (RCTHost.mm:621-644), the new view re-reads the flag, the new runtime re-reads the I18nManager constants (RCTI18nManager.mm:49-55). A JavaScript reload is enough; without it nothing changes until the next launch.
Android: isRTL = manifest supportsRtl AND (forceRTL OR (allowRTL AND Locale.getAvailableLocales()[0] is RTL)) - I18nUtil.kt:22-24, :55-69. In practice only the force flag counts. Re-read at every root measure (ReactSurfaceView.kt:83-117 -> ReactSurfaceImpl.kt:178-194), so the layout changes even before the reload; the reload refreshes the JS constant. No process restart needed.
expo-localization OnCreate runs at every start and every reload on both platforms (ModuleHolder.swift:56; AppContext.kt:139-141): iOS allowRTL(true) only (patched, LocalizationModule.swift:72); Android allowRTL(true) only (LocalizationModule.kt:55-72; the forcesRTL string stays "unset").

WHAT A MEMBER SEES
Fresh install, Arabic phone: iPhone is right-to-left from the first frame, no restart. Android draws left-to-right behind the splash, sets the flag, reloads once (the splash shows twice), then right-to-left.
Fresh install, English phone: the app opens in English, left-to-right (i18n/index.ts:68-77, :131-137). Choosing Arabic sets the flags and reloads: right-to-left at once and at every later launch.
Arabic phone, English chosen: Android left-to-right after the reload. iPhone right-to-left for ever (the hole above).
Between the choice and the reload: iPhone nothing changes; Android the layout can flip at the next root measure while the old language is still on screen.

MEASUREMENTS (working tree, app/src)
Text styles with a font: 730; without textAlign: 249; stretched usages without alignment (heuristic): 59 now, 62 in the members' tree (97705af).
`textDir(` call sites: 7 in the members' bundle (news only), 20 now.
`textAlign: 'left' | 'right'` literals: 1 (FormField.tsx:113, Latin inputs). Module-scope I18nManager.isRTL reads: 2 in the members' bundle (NewsCarousel.tsx:25, ProfileCompleteness.tsx:24), 0 now. `row-reverse`: 0. `direction: 'ltr'`: watch.tsx:347, :353 only.
TextInputs (8 components): members' bundle - CountryPicker search, OptionPicker search, contact composer on the physical left; projects search unaligned; FormField, advisor composer, code fields correct. Now - CountryPicker.tsx:173 and OptionPicker.tsx:130 still on the physical left.
ar.json, 1,614 strings: 2 open with a Latin letter (auth.login.placeholder, form.file.hint), 16 open with a placeholder, 10 are Latin only, 0 contain a line break. en.json: 3 strings contain Arabic (the language names).
One Text holding multi-line server or member text: contact.tsx:176, AdminPopup.tsx:85, WorkshopAd.tsx:108, (tabs)/news.tsx:157, meetup/[key].tsx:49, people/[id].tsx:68.

corrections: Most of the native mechanics hold up in the code. Android TextLayoutManager.kt:183-213 takes one alignment from the first strong letter of the whole string (FIRSTSTRONG_LTR). buildLayout (:661-694) sets no text direction, so every paragraph resolves its own direction. TextAttributeProps.kt:417 drops writingDirection. ReactTextInputManager.kt:562-563 maps 'left' to Gravity.LEFT. On iOS, RCTAttributedTextUtils.mm:197-216 swaps left and right only when an alignment is set, and the input's defaultTextAttributes come from props with no layoutDirection (RCTTextInputComponentView.mm:146-147, :295-300). ParagraphShadowNode.cpp:81-84 takes the text direction from Yoga.

The colleague's list of multi-line Text sites leaves out the most-used one: the AI advisor's replies. In the members' bundle (97705af:app/src/components/advisor/RichText.tsx:48-50, :80), every non-heading, non-table line is joined into ONE paragraph with '\n', and bullets are rewritten to '• '. That paragraph is drawn as one Text (MessageBubble style text: textAlign textStart, :204). On Android, any bullet line whose first strong letter is Latin ('• ROI: …', '• **SaaS**: …', '1. MVP …') is laid out LTR with ALIGN_NORMAL, so it sits at the LEFT edge between right-aligned Arabic bullets. On iPhone the line stays right-aligned, but the bullet and the Latin term sit at the left end of the line. The working tree still joins lines this way (RichText.tsx:129 plus flush). Its new contentDir (:18-21) sets only textAlign for Arabic text, so nothing changes on either platform.

Cause 2 says the M241 commit opened a message to every account. It did not: 7f4bca3 opens the management contact thread (/api/contact) to every signed-in account; it is not a broadcast text. contact.tsx:176 is still a valid multi-line site, but there is no M241 'Investors Club'-first message to point at.

Cause 4 / fix-plan step 3 says that switching textDir to textStart plus writingDirection 'still cures the M177 case'. On Android it does not. writingDirection is ignored there (TextAttributeProps.kt:417). An Arabic headline that opens with a Latin word becomes right-aligned (the ALIGN_OPPOSITE swap) but keeps LTR word order, with the Latin word at the left end of the line. Android needs a bidi mark in the string; the style alone cannot do it.

Cause 6 (English chosen on an Arabic iPhone stays RTL) is real in the code: LocalizationModule.swift:23-31 and :72 run allowRTL(true) at every start, and RCTI18nUtil.m:32-41 counts the app's language. But it produces the opposite of the complaint: English text pushed to the RIGHT. It only touches English-mode members on Arabic iPhones. It is not a lead for 'text pushed to the left'.
Cause 7 is speculative (a narrow race window) and does not explain a steady complaint.

Fix-plan step 2 (a ContentText component that splits strings into one Text per paragraph at about 25 sites) is more invasive than it needs to be. Inserting U+200F / U+200E at the start of each paragraph INSIDE the same string gives the same result on Android. The whole-string first-strong test then sees the mark, so the alignment is ALIGN_NORMAL, and each paragraph's own direction becomes the mark's direction. This keeps numberOfLines, ClampText measurement, Highlight and SarText spans and the selectable text intact.

Fix-plan step 4 (put textAlign: textStart into the shared typography tokens) has a hazard the colleague did not list. Any TextInput style that spreads a typography token and has no textAlign of its own would get 'left', which is the PHYSICAL left for an input. That would push Arabic input to the left, the very symptom being fixed. Composer and FormField do not spread tokens today, but the default is a trap. Use explicit per-style alignment instead.

Fix-plan step 5 (direction on the root container) does nothing for the complaint in the normal state, where the native flag already matches the language. Physical left/right styles and native components that follow the I18nManager flag (horizontal lists, gestures) would not follow a Yoga-only direction, so it adds risk for a rare edge. It is optional and goes last.

challenge.ownerMessage: Text that starts with an English word (advisor replies with terms like ROI or SaaS, Latin project and video names, management messages) makes the phone flip that line, so it jumps to the left edge, most often on Android. The country search box is also set to the wrong side. A small OTA update fixes this: it marks each line's direction inside the text, fixes the search boxes, and you decide whether English-only names stay on the right in Arabic mode. Only the English-on-an-Arabic-iPhone case needs the next store build, 1.3.4.
